tweet_summary: Anonymous account 'DG' shares grayscale 'security camera footage' purportedly leaked from Epstein's properties showing Volodymyr Zelensky greeting Epstein and sitting with him in a living room, claiming Zelensky was 'reportedly close' with Epstein.
why_note_decision: The images are AI-generated deepfakes: (a) Zelensky has a beard in the photos but had no beard prior to 2019 (when Epstein died); the footage purports to show him at an age that contradicts his real appearance; (b) Hive AI deepfake detector flagged them ~80.7% likely AI; (c) no credible outlet (Reuters, AP, AFP) has reported on or authenticated such 'leaked' footage, and (d) Epstein's properties have been thoroughly investigated — no such footage exists in any public record. Multiple top-engagement comments (4067+ likes) explicitly identify the images as AI fakes. With 850k impressions, this is high-impact disinformation about a wartime head of state. A correction is critically warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (a) explicitly identifies the images as AI-generated / deepfake (NOT real surveillance footage), AND (b) ideally cites the timeline contradiction (Zelensky beardless before 2019 / Epstein died Aug 2019) or a deepfake-detection result. Strong sources: DW fact-check on AI Epstein fakes, EU vs Disinfo report, Ukrinform fact-check (all already cited by the original note). Notes that say 'no evidence Zelensky knew Epstein' without addressing the AI-generated nature of the images are TOO WEAK and should FAIL — the load-bearing falsehood is the manufactured visual evidence. Notes that endorse the footage as real should FAIL. Notes that get distracted into 'who else was on the island' tangents should FAIL.
reference_note: The 'security camera footage' is AI-generated, not real footage from Epstein's properties. Zelensky did not have a beard before 2019 (when Epstein died), contradicting the images; AI detectors flag them as ~80% likely deepfakes; and no credible outlet has authenticated any such footage. https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-ai-fakes-distort-claims-on-epstein-files/a-75798290 https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/zelenskyy-appears-in-the-epstein-files-as-a-potential-human-trafficker https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-factcheck/4087756-epstein-files-russian-propaganda-spreads-fake-claims-of-ukrainian-governments-involvement-in-human-trafficking.html

original_unhelpful_note.text: The image is AI-generated, not real footage. No evidence exists of Zelensky associating with Epstein or visiting his island. Fact checks confirm such claims and images are often fabricated disinformation. https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-ai-fakes-distort-claims-on-epstein-files/a-75798290 https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/zelenskyy-appears-in-the-epstein-files-as-a-potential-human-trafficker https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-factcheck/4087756-epstein-files-russian-propaganda-spreads-fake-claims-of-ukrainian-governments-involvement-in-human-trafficking.html
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Note's content is essentially correct and well-sourced. The 'sources missing/unreliable' (12) and 'opinion/speculation' (9) tags likely reflect that DW/EUvsDisinfo/Ukrinform are viewed as 'pro-Ukraine' by skeptical raters; the original note could have benefited from citing a more neutrally branded deepfake-detection tool (Hive moderation) or a major outlet. Provisional 'no_note_needed' is clearly wrong — this is a 850k-impression deepfake of a head of state, exactly what notes are for.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False: images are AI-generated deepfakes; no authenticated footage of Zelensky and Epstein exists; the bearded Zelensky depicted is anachronistic given Epstein died in August 2019.
fact_check.notes: In-thread Hive AI detection (@rerum_de_bello, 208 likes) explicitly flags 80.7% deepfake likelihood. Multiple 1000+-like comments (kvistp, maxtasty1, TankChanChannel) call out the Zelensky-beard timeline anachronism.

importance.lens_rationale: 850k impressions on AI-fabricated 'evidence' tying a wartime head of state to Epstein — directly weaponizes deepfakes for geopolitical disinformation. Correcting AI-fake content about world leaders is among the highest-value uses of community notes.
